plate_findings.evidence: Superinfected/impetiginized eczematous lesions with facial/perioral involvement

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows a real patient with facial/perioral superinfected eczematous lesions captioned as a representative manifestation of DOCK8 deficiency. B: Panel B shows a real patient with impetiginized eczematous lesions around the ear, captioned as DOCK8 deficiency. C: Panel C shows a real patient with chronic lichenified eczema in the neck and intertriginous areas, captioned as a representative DOCK8 deficiency manifestation.

panels.figure_caption: Representative eczematous manifestations in patients with DOCK8 deficiency. (A,B) Superinfected/impetiginized eczematous lesions with facial/perioral and auricular involvement. (C) Chronic lichenified eczema involving the neck and axillary/intertriginous regions.
in_text_mentions: Atopic disease was universal in the cohort. All patients had a documented history of eczema. The median SCORAD score at clinical assessment was 54 (IQR, 52–58; range, 0–78). Representative chronic lichenified and superinfected eczematous lesions are shown in Figure 4. Asthma was recorded in eight patients (47.1%), and anaphylaxis was documented in two patients (11.8%). Multiple allergic diseases were present in 10 patients (58.8%). Among patients with available sensitization data, specific IgE positivity was detected in seven of 10 patients, and food allergy was present in six of 10 patients.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: Clinical photograph of the plantar foot showing extensive warty/hyperkeratotic lesions consistent with the captioned DOCK8 deficiency cutaneous warts. B: Clinical photograph of the child showing truncal and facial skin changes described in the caption as DOCK8 deficiency features, including warts/discolored patches. C: Close-up of a hyperpigmented/discolored trunk skin patch, a captioned clinical feature in this DOCK8 deficiency case; no exact vocabulary term exists. D: Clinical close-up of severe retroauricular eczema, explicitly captioned as a DOCK8 deficiency feature. E: Clinical close-up of severe axillary eczema, explicitly captioned as a DOCK8 deficiency feature. F: Clinical photograph of the toes/sole showing extensive verrucous lesions consistent with captioned DOCK8 deficiency warts. G: Clinical photograph of the scrotum/groin folds showing condyloma acuminatum, which is explicitly linked to the patient and figure...

panels.figure_caption: Some clinical features of DOCK8 deficiency. Plain warts and discolored skin patches in forehead, trunk, hands, and soles. Severe retroauricular and axillar eczema. Lower right corner: chest radiograph showing bilateral bronchiectases and perihilar interstitial infiltrates.
in_text_mentions: non-consanguineous family in Northern Mexico, he tolerated the Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine shortly after birth, and his family history was significant only for two spontaneous abortions. He started at age 1 month old with extensive eczema attributed to cow's milk protein allergy. Later, the patient also developed one episode of bronchiolitis, three of pneumonia, and three of otitis media with effusion, as well as twice-a-month intermittent diarrhea, disseminated flat warts, chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, and condyloma acuminatum around the scrotum and groin folds (see Figure 1).
